title: The Pulse Above the Rafters
story: The Archive Nook had grown familiar, but the library was never entirely silent. James knew the sound of paper breathing in the draft. James knew the sound of rain tapping like small fingernails against the round window. James knew the distant creak of the front doors opening to the morning. But as twilight pooled in the high corners of the ceiling, a new rhythm shuddered through the timber beams: a deep, deliberate tick-clack, followed by the low groan of winding iron cable. It was a sound that tasted of oil and brass, pulling a memory from his very first night in Oakhaven when he had sat beside a warm hearth surrounded by swinging pendulums. James gathered his leather strap, adjusting the canister bound in Mateo's colorful threads, and checked that his clay whistle was nestled securely in place. Following the rhythmic vibration along the topmost catwalk, he discovered a narrow spiral stair of pierced iron tucked behind the leather-bound annals—a stair that curled steeply upward into the heart of the library's central dome. At the top of the stair stood the Great Clockwork. Massive interlocking wheels of gleaming brass and blackened iron turned in stately, unhurried circles, their teeth catching with heavy precision. And there, perched on a wooden stool with a smudge of grease on his knuckle and a slender brass oiler in hand, was Barnaby. When the old clockmaker turned and saw James emerge into the lantern light, his face broke into a familiar, crinkling smile. Barnaby did not ask where James had traveled, but his eyes rested with quiet understanding on the indigo wool and the clay whistle tucked into James's pack. Reaching into his leather apron, the clockmaker produced a tiny brass cog—smooth, unthreaded, its five teeth worn round like a star—and offered it on an open palm. Every great machine needs a spare tooth to remember where to begin, Barnaby murmured softly, his voice matching the steady tempo of the escapement wheel. James took the small cog, its cool metal warming instantly against his fingers, and tucked it safely alongside his seed pod. Together, they sat on the high wooden bench in companionable silence, listening as the heartbeat of Oakhaven echoed down into the darkening town below.
location: The Clock Tower Loft, Grand Library, Oakhaven
